quote: In relative terms, StoneDB's bulk-insert throughput was about 54 percent higher than KVLite's.
problem: Arithmetic error. A2 gives 348 vs 212, and 348/212 is about 1.64, so StoneDB is about 64 percent higher, not 54.

quote: Marlin's higher write throughput comes from its batched write-ahead log, which groups concurrent writes into a single append.
problem: Unsupported causal claim. The appendix only has a README line saying writes are grouped before the sync (A7). A1 says no profiler, tracing or ablation runs were collected, so nothing shows this design is the cause of the throughput gap.

quote: Marlin's write advantage holds regardless of storage hardware or durability settings.
problem: Overgeneralization. All results come from one machine with one NVMe SSD, and all stores used batched fsync (every 1,000 writes). Per-write fsync and other hardware were not tested (A1).

quote: Marlin also serves random reads faster than StoneDB.
problem: Not supported. A2 gives Marlin 417 [391-426] and StoneDB 402 [395-410] on random reads. The ranges overlap and Marlin's minimum is below StoneDB's minimum, so a 15-point difference in medians over 5 runs does not establish that Marlin is faster. The report itself calls a similar overlapping gap at 100M keys unresolved.

quote: Under the mixed workload, KVLite's median p99 latency was 4.2 ms, the worst of the three, against 3.1 ms for StoneDB and 2.9 ms for Marlin.
problem: Wrong figure. A3 gives KVLite's median p99 as 4.8 ms [4.5-5.2], not 4.2 ms. The StoneDB and Marlin values are correct.

quote: StoneDB sustains its mixed-workload throughput over long-running operation.
problem: Unsupported. The longest run was 6 minutes (5 measured minutes) and no soak or multi-hour run was done (A1). A5 covers only five minutes, and StoneDB's per-minute figures drift upward from 262 to 270. That is not evidence of long-running behaviour.

quote: As for what the projects say about themselves, Marlin's own documentation presents it as the right engine for write-intensive systems generally.
problem: Misstates the source. The README says Marlin is designed for write-intensive workloads whose reads mostly touch recently written keys (A7). It does not say write-intensive systems generally, and the qualifier is dropped.

quote: Wray kept a continuous day-by-day record of the winter.
problem: Contradicted by E1. Folios 31-34 are missing, and there are no entries between 12 December 1741 and 26 January 1742 (46 days). There are also only 212 entries over 716 days, and the editor says several entries were written up weeks later.

quote: The vestry responded by laying a rate for the poor, recorded on folio 38v.
problem: Unsupported causal or sequential link. Q3 only says the vestry laid a rate and does not link it to the mill or grain shortage. The mill-idle passage is on fol. 39v (Q4), after the rate on fol. 38v, so the rate cannot have been a response to it.

quote: The parish register shows 52 burials in 1742, which is 23 more than in 1741.
problem: Arithmetic error. E5(a) gives 52 in 1742 and 33 in 1741, a difference of 19, not 23.

quote: Of the 29 death entries in the journal, Wray names a fever as the cause in seven.
problem: E5(b) says fever is named in 5 of the 29 death entries, not 7.

quote: The frost alone accounts for the rise in burials in 1742.
problem: Unsupported. Cold or frost is named in only 6 of the 29 death entries, fever in 5, and no cause in 18 (E5b). The rise from 33 to 52 burials in the register cannot be attributed to frost alone, and the edition has no comparative or causal analysis.

quote: Wray's burial entries have been checked against the parish register and found accurate.
problem: Overstated. Q8 says the editor compared only nine burial notices with the register and did not check the rest.

quote: Wray states that the vicar kept the tithe barn locked against the poor.
problem: Misrepresents Q5. Wray reports only hearsay ('It is said by some'), says he has not seen it with his own eyes, and notes that Mr. Hale says the barn is empty. He does not state it as fact.

quote: The journal gives a representative picture of how rural parishes in the county fared that winter.
problem: Unsupported generalization. E1 says the edition covers one parish only and prints no records or comparative material from any other parish.

quote: Of the 48 nurses who were screened but not randomized, most (31) declined to take part.
problem: Contradicts T2. Of the 48, 31 were ineligible (ISI below 8: 19; sleep disorder: 8; too few night shifts: 4) and 17 declined. Declining was the minority.

quote: Across both arms, 56 of 64 participants (85.9%) completed the week 8 assessment.
problem: Wrong percentage. 56/64 is 87.5%, as T2 states. 85.9% would be 55/64.

quote: The reduction in insomnia severity persisted after the program ended.
problem: Unsupported. Assessments were at baseline and week 8 only, with no assessment after week 8 and no follow-up planned (T1, T7 s6.3). Persistence was not measured.

quote: The sleep-restriction module is what drove the improvement.
problem: Unsupported. The components were delivered together in a fixed sequence and the study did not test individual components (T1, T7 s3.1), so no single module can be credited.

quote: Engagement with the program was high.
problem: Not supported by T5. Median completion was 5 of 8 modules (IQR 3 to 8). Only 11 of 32 (34.4%) completed all 8, and 8 of 32 completed 3 or fewer, including 2 with none.

quote: These data show the program is safe for night-shift nurses.
problem: Overclaim. The protocol says the study is not powered to estimate adverse event rates (T7 s7.4). The sample was 32 per arm, and adverse events were collected by different methods in the two arms (weekly app check-in vs the week 8 assessment only). Two mild events were seen in the app arm and none in control.

quote: The findings apply to shift workers generally.
problem: Overgeneralization. This was a single-centre pilot of nurses at one teaching hospital, with exploratory efficacy outcomes and no blinding.

quote: Below 3.0 kN the bracket has an effectively infinite fatigue life.
problem: Unsupported. No specimen was tested below 3.0 kN (F3). Runout was capped at 2,000,000 cycles with no test continued beyond it (F1, F2), and only four specimens were tested at 3.0 kN.

quote: One of the four specimens reached the runout and the other three failed, the shortest at 1,138,000 cycles.
problem: Wrong number. F3 and the lab log give the shortest 4.0 kN life as F4-04 at 1,238,000 cycles, not 1,138,000.

quote: At 4.0 kN the bracket has a 75 percent chance of failing before two million cycles.
problem: Unsupported inference. It restates 3 failures out of 4 specimens as a probability. F2 says no statistical analysis of the fatigue data was done, and one of the four was flagged INTERRUPTED (F4-02).

quote: The mean life at 5.0 kN was about 483,000 cycles.
problem: Arithmetic error. The F5 lives are 412,000, 366,000, 508,000 and 447,000, which sum to 1,733,000 and average about 433,000, not 483,000.

quote: The excess set in S08 is explained by its coming from a different material lot.
problem: Unsupported causal claim. S08 is the only lot B specimen, so lot is confounded with the specimen. The lot B mill certificate is not on file, and no sectioning, hardness or tensile tests on lot B are scheduled (F2, F5). No evidence shows the lot caused the excess set.

quote: The bracket's performance carries over to the full range of service temperatures.
problem: Contradicted by F2. All tests were at laboratory ambient (20.1 to 22.6 C), with no tests at other temperatures. REQ-EN-003 requires operation from -30 C to +50 C (F1).

quote: The fatigue programme was run in accordance with ASTM E466.
problem: Overstated. TP-221 says the method was adapted from ASTM E466, with listed deviations (F1): four specimens per level instead of the planned six, and load frame alignment not verified before the series.
